topics.title: Feminism, Sex and Gender
topics.benchmark_preservation: The approved design reference, prior topic artifacts and canonical Political Theory owners remain immutable.

panels.panel_title: Patriarchy, Feminism and the Central Political Question
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Patriarchy, Feminism and the Central Political Question
[1] Gauba treats feminism as a protest against the inferior status assigned to women by
patriarchy, not as a denial that biological differences exist. (PDF pp.84-86)
v
[2] The sex-gender distinction is central for answering why inequality can be socially
constructed even when biological difference is real. (PDF pp.84-86)
v
[3] The three streams of feminism provide a compact framework for PSIR and GS-II answers
on equality, citizenship and justice. (PDF pp.88-90)
v
[4] The topic teaches how power can operate through family roles, labour division,
culture and political exclusion, not only through law or property. (PDF pp.85-87)
v
SYNTHESIS -> Patriarchy, Feminism and the Central Political Question is best presented through
its central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Sex, Gender and the Social Construction of Hierarchy
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Sex, Gender and the Social Construction of Hierarchy
[1] Gender roles such as aggressiveness/dominance for men and
submissiveness/expressiveness for women are treated as cultural instruments of
social control. (PDF p.85)
v
[2] Patriarchy: literally rule of the father, now used for wider male domination in
household, labour market and social life. (PDF p.84)
v
[3] Gender: culturally constructed images, expectations and status-distinctions attached
to women and men. (PDF pp.84-85)
v
[4] Gender inequality: a conventional or cultural inequality, hence open to criticism
and change. (PDF p.86)
v
[5] He then distinguishes sex from gender so that biological difference is separated
from socially assigned inferiority. (PDF pp.84-86)
v
SYNTHESIS -> Sex, Gender and the Social Construction of Hierarchy is best presented through
its central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Core Distinctions, Thinkers and Feminist Streams
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Core Distinctions, Thinkers and Feminist Streams
[1] Shulamith Firestone: radical feminist who ties women's subordination to reproductive
biology and seeks release from that dependence through technological change. (PDF
v
[2] Kate Millett: radical feminist who interprets the relation between sexes as a power
relation sustained by ideology. (PDF p.89)
v
[3] Sheila Rowbotham: socialist feminist linking women's liberation with struggle
against capitalism and other oppressions. (PDF pp.89-90)
v
[4] Natural inequality vs conventional inequality: Gauba uses Rousseau's distinction to
show that gender inequality belongs to the alterable second category. (PDF p.86)
v
[5] Legal equality vs substantive equality: early feminism attacked barriers to
education, property and vote; later feminism asks whether equal law alone changes
social power. (PDF pp.88-91)
v
SYNTHESIS -> Core Distinctions, Thinkers and Feminist Streams is best presented through its
central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Illustrations, Comparative Matrix and Trap Repair
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Illustrations, Comparative Matrix and Trap Repair
[1] Gauba's examples of girls being socialized toward obedience and boys toward
assertiveness show how gender roles are culturally produced. (PDF p.87)
v
[2] The early rights agenda focused on education, property, divorce and suffrage because
these exclusions had no necessary connection with female biology. (PDF pp.87-88)
v
[3] A safe classroom example is to contrast biological maternity with culturally
assigned ideas that women must therefore remain outside public life.
v
SYNTHESIS -> Illustrations, Comparative Matrix and Trap Repair is best presented through its
central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Ownership Boundaries, Revision Spine and Source Discipline
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Ownership Boundaries, Revision Spine and Source Discipline
[1] Primary source used directly: O. P. Gauba, An Introduction to Political Theory,
Fifth Edition (2009), Ch.2, PDF pp.84-93.
v
[2] Use Rousseau's natural/conventional inequality distinction to show why gender
hierarchy is alterable. (PDF p.86)
v
[3] Classify feminism into liberal, radical and socialist streams with one thinker each.
v
[4] End by warning against using Gauba's dated numerical claims as present-day evidence.
v
[5] Key anchors: feminism, patriarchy, sex-gender distinction (PDF pp.84-86);
socialization and inequality (PDF pp.86-87); Wollstonecraft, Mill and three streams
of feminism (PDF pp.88-90).
v
SYNTHESIS -> Ownership Boundaries, Revision Spine and Source Discipline is best presented
through its central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.
CENTRAL FOCUS
Later Provenance and Marxist Feminism
[1] Exam use: if a question specifically says "Marxist feminism," lead with the
domestic-labour/social-reproduction claim; if it says "socialist feminism," lead
with Rowbotham's dual-systems synthesis; the two labels overlap but are not simple
synonyms.
v
[2] Gauba's chapter grounds the sex/gender distinction and the liberal/radical/socialist
typology; it does not itself discuss Simone de Beauvoir, Gayle Rubin, Ann Oakley,
Carole Pateman, Susan Moller Okin, Judith Butler or Kimberlé Crenshaw. Everything
below is a standard PSIR/political-theory extension used by examiners beyond this
specific book, flagged throughout, and is not tied to a page number in the primary
source.
v
[3] Ann Oakley (Sex, Gender and Society, 1972) is usually credited with popularising the
working sex/gender terminology in sociology — sex as biological, gender as the
culturally learned, historically variable content attached to that biology.
v
[4] Claim: women's oppression is generated principally by the capitalist mode of
production, especially unpaid domestic/reproductive labour that reproduces the
workforce free of charge.
v
SYNTHESIS -> Later Provenance and Marxist Feminism is best presented through its central
claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Pateman and Okin: Contract, Justice and the Family
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Pateman and Okin: Contract, Justice and the Family
[1] Susan Moller Okin (Justice, Gender, and the Family, 1989): Claim — theories of
justice (she targets Rawls) wrongly treat the family as a pre-political given rather
than a site justice must examine. Evidence — unequal domestic burden restricts
women's access to the "primary goods" (time, income, position) public justice is
meant to distribute. Significance — extends justice from state/market into the
household. Limit — risks over-extending justice into every private relationship,
which is why most syntheses still preserve some sphere of family autonomy alongside
gender-just background conditions.
v
SYNTHESIS -> Pateman and Okin: Contract, Justice and the Family is best presented through its
central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.
CENTRAL FOCUS
Butler, Performativity and Intersectionality
[1] Judith Butler (Gender Trouble, 1990): gender is not a cultural coating on a stable
biological sex but performative — produced through repeated, stylised acts (speech,
gesture, dress, behaviour) that create the appearance of a natural gendered self; on
this account even "sex" is partly constituted through gendered discourse, not a
wholly pre-discursive bedrock.
v
SYNTHESIS -> Butler, Performativity and Intersectionality is best presented through its
central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Objection-Reply Chains and Cautious Indian Application
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Objection-Reply Chains and Cautious Indian Application
[1] Objection: if gender is entirely performative/socially constructed (Butler),
feminism loses a stable category of "woman" around which to organise and to claim
rights. Reply: many feminist theorists respond that political claims can be built on
provisionally, strategically stabilised categories even while accepting the category
is historically constructed ("strategic essentialism"); legal sex-discrimination
categories function pragmatically regardless of deeper philosophical instability.
Present as a live, contested debate — not a settled result.
v
[2] Objection: radical feminism's emphasis on patriarchy as the primary, near-universal
structure of oppression risks treating "women" as one undifferentiated class,
erasing differences of race, class and caste among women. Reply: Crenshaw's
intersectionality and Marxist/socialist feminism's attention to class supply the
corrective — oppression is compounded and differently configured across axes,
producing a more accurate map of whose subordination is being explained. This reply
strengthens rather than replaces the original radical-feminist insight that
sexual/reproductive domination is analytically distinct from class or race
domination.
v
SYNTHESIS -> Objection-Reply Chains and Cautious Indian Application is best presented through
its central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.

panels.panel_title: Directive Decoding and Mark-Scaled Answer Architecture
lines: CENTRAL FOCUS
Directive Decoding and Mark-Scaled Answer Architecture
[1] "Distinguish sex and gender" → definitional/analytical directive: give the
distinction plus why it matters, not two one-line definitions.
v
[2] "Discuss/Examine feminism as a critique of patriarchy" → needs both diagnosis (what
patriarchy is, how gender is produced) and the feminist reply; do not describe
patriarchy without the feminist response.
v
[3] "Critically examine feminist perspectives on X" → requires thesis + at least two
schools compared + at least one objection/reply, ending in a reasoned verdict, not a
neutral list.
v
[4] Thesis (1-2 lines): feminism protests patriarchal subordination via the sex/gender
distinction; formal legal equality alone is insufficient.
v
[5] Body: sex vs gender (claim→evidence→significance) + one stream
(liberal/radical/socialist/Marxist) with its core mechanism.
v
SYNTHESIS -> Directive Decoding and Mark-Scaled Answer Architecture is best presented through
its central claim, causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.
CENTRAL FOCUS
MCQ Remediation and Trap Repair
[1] Feminism: concern with the status and role of women in relation to men, combined
with protest against injustice suffered because of sex.
v
[2] Patriarchy: literally rule of the father, now used for wider male domination in
household, labour market and social life.
v
[3] Sex: biological difference, such as reproductive function and secondary
characteristics.
v
[4] Gender: culturally constructed images, expectations and status-distinctions attached
to women and men.
v
SYNTHESIS -> MCQ Remediation and Trap Repair is best presented through its central claim,
causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.
CENTRAL FOCUS
PYQ Ownership and Answer Practice
[1] Butler's Gender Trouble argues gender is constituted through performative repetition
of stylised acts within a regulatory, discursive frame -- there is no gendered
substance prior to or behind the repeated acts. This treats gender as thoroughly
cultural: produced, disciplined, and reproduced through social practice, in contrast
to sex, which denotes a biological given. The cultural-category reading explains
variation across societies and time in what counts as masculine or feminine, which a
purely biological account cannot.
v
[2] Formal equality demands the removal of explicit differential rules; substantive
equality goes further, licensing affirmative measures to correct unequal starting
points; relational equality asks whether social relationships remain hierarchical
regardless of formal rules. Empowerment, on Kabeer's tripartite model, requires
resources, agency, and achievements -- it is the process by which formal or
substantive equality is actually converted into lived capacity. On this reading,
equality supplies the normative target and empowerment supplies the causal mechanism
by which that target is reached.
v
SYNTHESIS -> PYQ Ownership and Answer Practice is best presented through its central claim,
causal logic, strongest limit and qualified verdict.
EXAM ROUTE -> define precisely -> explain the mechanism -> test the limit ->
conclude with a qualified political judgment.
